label: conj:frobenius-antipode-unifies-chirality-and-tower
title: Frobenius antipode $S\colon \sigma \leftrightarrow \sigma^{-1}$ unifies chirality (Term 5) and neutron-tower closure
html:
Over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], q) carries the Kazhdan--Lusztig bar-semilinear anti-involution S(\sigma_i) = \sigma_i^{-1}, S(q) = q^{-1} (no \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]-linear anti-endomorphism sends \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} away from q = \pm 1, since (\sigma_i^{-1})^2 - h\sigma_i^{-1} - 1 = -2h\sigma_i^{-1} for h = q - q^{-1}, whereas bar-semilinearity sends h \mapsto -h and intertwines \mathrm{tr}_{M,q}(\sigma_i^{-1}) = z(q^{-1}) = q^{-4} z(q) for z(q) = q^3/(q^2+1)). This bar anti-involution unifies two derivations:

  1. The chirality factor a_K measures the symmetric-channel asymmetry under S.
  2. The neutron-tower closure evaluates the bar-symmetrization \hat V_0^{\mathrm{Frob}} := \tfrac{1}{2}(\hat V_0 + \hat V_0\circ S) of the per-generator volumes.

The single operator S spans both the parity splitting and the mass correction, fixing the bar-self-dual interface combination \tfrac{1}{2}(\sigma_i + \sigma_i^{-1}) = \sigma_i - \tfrac{1}{2}h while swapping positive and negative crossing chiralities.
heading: Conjecture
